subject: TidalBurst production: surge in latency and 5xx — request cross-region reroute

messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@tidalburst.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: alerts@tidalburst.ai, ops@tidalburst.ai
Date: 2028-09-03T07:42:00Z
Subject: High error rate + latency spike impacting inference - prod-usw2

Karthik —

We're seeing a sudden, sustained spike in p95 latency and 5xx rates across our production tenant in us-west-2 (TidalBurst account). Surface metrics: average p95 jumped from ~280ms to ~1.8s over the last 12 minutes, 5xx rate ~6.5% (spiking to 9% on some routes), and overall successful QPS has dropped by ~48%. No recent config pushes on our side.

Customers are reporting timeouts in the inference pipeline and the spike started ~07:30 UTC. Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing regional degradation or an AZ-level problem? Our app is latency-sensitive and we'd like Redwood to initiate a cross-region failover if you recommend it — please call out any impacts (cache warmup, embedding state).

We need a short update ASAP (status + next steps) and an authorization request if you need permission to switch routing.

Attachments: none on our side (we can share traces if you want).

—Maya
Maya Rao
Head of Platform Ops, TidalBurst AI
maya.rao@tidalburst.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@tidalburst.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-09-03T07:56:00Z
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency spike impacting inference - prod-usw2

Thanks for the heads-up, Maya — we're on it.

Immediate notes: our telemetry shows a concentrated error amplification in us-west-2 affecting model-serving nodes on az-west-2b (unusual connection resets on the GPU host layer). We're already seeing degraded KV-cache hit rates which explains the latency amplification. Engineering will attempt a controlled cross-region reroute to us-east-1 to keep latency bounded while we triage the AZ.

Requesting your authorization to perform an application-level reroute (region-level steering) for the TidalBurst production routes; expected short-term impacts: cold KV caches for ~2–6min on some hot prefixes and transient token-rate skew. We will not change model versions and will preserve request headers for routing.

I've attached a quick triage dump from our edge (triage-output-20280903.txt) and will send a log of the reroute steps once complete.

Next steps (short timeline):
- 07:58 UTC: engineering to start staged reroute (2% -> 25% -> 100% if stable).
- 08:05 UTC: monitor error rate and p95; revert if 5xx > 3% or p95 > 1.2s
- 08:30 UTC: post-change status update + customer comms draft

Please reply with AUTH or NO-AUTH. If we don't hear within 10 minutes we'll hold off and continue with mitigations inside the AZ.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Manager — Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: URGENT: Authorization for TidalBurst region steer — exec attention

Karthik / Dylan —

Quick engineering update from SRE and serving runtime: we executed a staged region reroute as planned (2% -> 25% -> 100%) beginning at 07:58 UTC. Observed behavior:
- 07:59 UTC: first-stage (2%) showed 5xx drop from 7.1% -> 3.6%
- 08:06 UTC: at 25% we saw p95 improve to ~820ms and 5xx ~2.8%
- 08:14 UTC: we pushed to 100% for TidalBurst traffic to us-east-1; KV cache cold-start resulted in a short p50 blip (350ms -> 1.1s) but p95 settled ~620ms within 3m.

Actions taken:
- Drained affected nodes in us-west-2 az-west-2b and flagged hosts for deeper hardware/network review.
- Enabled short-lived request-level caching for the warm-up window to reduce retries.
- Kept model variant and token limits unchanged.

Current status (08:30 UTC): error rate trending down at 1.9%, p95 ~610–700ms, QPS restored to ~92% of baseline. We'll hold the region steer for 60 minutes and re-evaluate at 09:25 UTC.

Notes for comms: include the cause as "AZ-level host instability leading to degraded cache hit rate" and the mitigation as "controlled region-level steering to us-east-1 with minimal consumer impact; caches warming for ~2–6min".

—Rachel Kim
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-09-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: High error rate + latency spike impacting inference - prod-usw2 — actions and next steps

Hi Maya — thanks again for the alert and patience.

Summary of what we did (complete):
- Identified AZ-level instability in us-west-2 (az-west-2b) that was causing host resets and KV-cache collapse.
- Per your authorization, executed controlled region-level reroute of production traffic to us-east-1 (07:58–08:14 UTC staged rollout).
- Result: error rate reduced to ~1.9% and p95 improved to ~610–700ms; QPS restored to ~92% of pre-incident levels.

Next steps:
- SRE will perform hardware/network forensic on drained hosts in az-west-2b and post a remediation plan by EOD.
- We'll hold the region reroute for 60 minutes, then test reintroducing traffic in small batches to us-west-2 once host health is validated.
- We'll prepare a short incident summary + postmortem (postmortem-skeleton.md attached) and offer a one-time credit for customer impact over 45 minutes per our credit policy (dylan is leading).

If you want immediate rollback to us-west-2 while we validate, we can coordinate a staged return — otherwise we will continue to hold in us-east-1 until 09:25 UTC evaluation.

Comms draft (customer-facing):

We are validating host health and will follow up with a timeline for returning traffic and a short postmortem. Thank you for the quick report; we will share remediation details shortly.

Please confirm preferred rollback behavior or ACK to hold the reroute.

Best,
